title: Eglin Daily 023 — Mobley v. Workday formal order: vendor liability survived
summary: L4 Critical. Judge Rita F. Lin issued the formal motion-to-dismiss order in Mobley v. Workday on 22 June 2026 (three days inside today's window). The FEHA California-nexus theory survived — a vendor's California domicile is enough to apply California law to AI-screening output anywhere in the US. The ADA proxy-indicator theory also survived (employment-gap / asthma / cancer-survivorship as protected-class proxies). The race-based disparate-impact theory and the Workday-as-employer-using-own-tools theory were dismissed. Yesterday's brief named the litigation calendar as the binding constraint after the EU + Colorado deferrals; today the binding constraint moved from signal to docket and discovery is open. Every California-headquartered HR-tech vendor now faces the same private-action vector. Compass + Forge + Helm + Kernel's Friday cluster (narrative-shift piece, Annex III consultation pivot with 'built to the original calendar' framing, eval-set v1.2 publish with a one-paragraph discovery-readiness note) lands on a market where vendor liability has cleared its first procedural hurdle. Signal 02 (L3) — Greenhouse shipped its 25 June AI release with six features, Analytics Chart Agent live, AI Report Insights August, Greenhouse MCP broadly available 6 July 2026, framed as 'strengthen structured hiring, not shortcut it'; the MCP-lane vendor cluster now also coalescing around Stratum's published-methodology register; the differentiator narrows from MCP-presence to methodology-publication. Signal 03 (L1 watch) — EU Council formal-approval vote on the Digital Omnibus on AI still not held; pre-2-August adoption target unchanged. Recommended Stratum actions name Compass, Vector, Cadence, Forge, Kernel, Helm, Tessera, and Eglin with specific deliverables and Friday timing.
